$comment: Environment identity — the one place a deployed environment's provider IDs are named: its Supabase project, its Render API service, and the Vercel team and projects both environments deploy to. These are NOT secrets: the Supabase project refs already appear in docs/ops/db-rollback-playbook.md, docs/internal/environment/CLOUD_SANDBOX.md and .claude/skills/live-verification/SKILL.md, a ref alone grants nothing without SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, and the Render and Vercel ids grant nothing without RENDER_API_KEY or VERCEL_API_KEY. What IS a secret is the token, and that still comes from Infisical or the GitHub environment. Read this file through scripts/ci/lib/environments.mjs rather than parsing it inline; a workflow reads the provider ids through scripts/ci/provider-ids.mjs, and no workflow names one as a literal (#2806; a test greps for them). `infisicalEnvSlug` values are Infisical SLUGS, not display names — production is `prod`, not `production`; scripts/check-env-slugs.mjs scans this file for exactly that trap. `renderDeploySource` says how the deploy job ships that environment's API: `commit` (Render builds the commit; a git-backed service) or `image` (the job builds the image on GitHub, pushes it to `apiImage` on GitHub's container registry, and Render pulls it; an image-backed service, #2506). It moves with `renderServiceId`, because Render cannot turn one kind of service into the other. Only staging may be `image` so far: production's deploy builds its image for Cloud Run alone and pushes none to `apiImage`, so provider-ids.mjs refuses it there before anything is applied. `apiHost` says where the API runs: `render` (the service above) or `cloud-run` (#5228). `cloudRun` names the environment's Google Cloud project, its number and region, and the service's instance bounds; the service, registry, accounts and sign-in provider are the names scripts/gcp/bootstrap.sh gives every project, so environments.mjs derives them rather than this file repeating them. Both environments are `cloud-run` since #5228; production's Render service stays as the rollback until Render is removed. Optional per-environment flag: `allowEmptyMigrationHistory` (default false) tells check-migration-order.mjs that an empty applied-migration list is legitimate rather than a wrong ref — set it only for a genuinely new project, since both projects here permanently hold 00000000000000_initial_schema.
